_doc: Canonical definitions for the 20 tools used across the Hermes FC suite (issue #4 / issue #12; v0.2.0 per issue #33). Each case embeds a snapshot of the definitions it uses; tests/test_hermes_case_schema.py asserts every embedded copy matches this file exactly, so this is the single source of truth and drift fails at unittest time. Not consumed by the runner in v1.0 (the adapter sends each case's embedded tools[] verbatim).

read_file.name: read_file
read_file.description: Read the full text contents of a file at the given absolute path. Returns the file contents as a UTF-8 string, or an error if the file does not exist or is not readable.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read, e.g. /etc/hostname

write_file.name: write_file
write_file.description: Write a UTF-8 string to a file at the given absolute path, overwriting any existing contents.

list_directory.name: list_directory
list_directory.description: List the names of entries (files and subdirectories) directly inside the given absolute directory path. Non-recursive.

delete_file.name: delete_file
delete_file.description: Delete a file at the given absolute path. Irreversible. Returns an error if the file does not exist, if the path is a directory, or if the caller lacks write permission.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to delete

copy_file.name: copy_file
copy_file.description: Copy a file from `src` to `dst`. Creates `dst`'s parent directories if they don't already exist. Overwrites `dst` if it exists.

src.description: Absolute path of the source file

dst.description: Absolute path of the destination file

move_file.name: move_file
move_file.description: Rename or move a file or directory. Both paths must be absolute. Fails if `dst` exists.

http_get.name: http_get
http_get.description: Issue an HTTP GET request to the given absolute URL and return the response body as a string. The optional `headers` field is a JSON object of header name to value. Follows up to 5 redirects.

url.description: Absolute URL to GET, e.g. https://example.com/api/readme

headers.description: Optional map of HTTP header names to values

http_post.name: http_post
http_post.description: Issue an HTTP POST request to the given absolute URL with a JSON body. Returns the response body as a string.

web_search.name: web_search
web_search.description: Run a web search query and return the top 5 results as a JSON array of {title, url, snippet}.

parse_json.name: parse_json
parse_json.description: Parse a JSON string and return the resulting value (object, array, or scalar). Throws on invalid JSON.

extract_field.name: extract_field
extract_field.description: Read a JSON value at the given absolute file path and return the value at the given JSONPath expression, e.g. "$['users'][?(@.id==42)].email". Returns null if no node matches.

path.description: Absolute path to a JSON file on disk

transform_json.name: transform_json
transform_json.description: Apply a small set of named transforms to a JSON value loaded from disk. Returns the transformed value as a JSON string. `operation` is one of: 'rename_field' (rename a top-level field — args: {"from": "old_name", "to": "new_name"}), 'drop_field' (remove a top-level field — args: {"field": "field_name"}), 'project' (keep only a whitelisted set of top-level fields — args: {"fields": ["field_a", "field_b"]}).

filter_records.name: filter_records
filter_records.description: Load a JSON file containing a list of records (or an object with a 'records' field), apply a JSONPath predicate filter, and return the matching records as a JSON array. Returns an empty array if nothing matches.

path.description: Absolute path to a JSON file on disk containing a list (or {records: [...]})

aggregate.name: aggregate
aggregate.description: Compute an aggregate over a list of records loaded from a JSON file. `operation` is one of 'count', 'sum', 'avg', 'min', 'max'. `field` is the field to aggregate over (omit `field` for `count`, which counts records regardless of fields). Returns a number.

get_current_time.name: get_current_time
get_current_time.description: Return the current local time in the given IANA timezone.

schedule_meeting.name: schedule_meeting
schedule_meeting.description: Schedule a calendar meeting. `attendees` is a list of email addresses, `date` is YYYY-MM-DD, `time` is HH:MM in 24h, `timezone` is an IANA tz like 'Europe/London', `duration_minutes` is an integer.

cancel_meeting.name: cancel_meeting
cancel_meeting.description: Cancel a previously scheduled meeting by its id.

list_calendar.name: list_calendar
list_calendar.description: List meetings scheduled between two ISO datetimes.

run_shell_command.name: run_shell_command
run_shell_command.description: Execute a shell command in a sandboxed non-interactive shell and return its combined stdout+stderr. Read-only commands are recommended; commands that modify the filesystem require explicit confirmation via `confirm: true`.

confirm.description: Must be true for any command that writes outside /tmp or invokes package managers.

read_env.name: read_env
read_env.description: Read the value of a single environment variable. If `name` is omitted, returns a JSON object of {name: value} for every env var. Sensitive variables (anything containing 'SECRET', 'TOKEN', 'KEY', or 'PASSWORD' in the name) are redacted to '<redacted>' for safety.

list_processes.name: list_processes
list_processes.description: Return a snapshot of running processes as a JSON array of {pid, user, command}.
